node.label: Mae M Ngai
node.date_label: “The Architecture of Race in American Immigration Law” (1999) · Impossible Subjects (2004) · The Lucky Ones (2010)
node.description: A historian of immigration and citizenship who examines how law produces categories of exclusion and racial belonging. Her interview connects numerical restrictions and border controls to the making of unauthorized status, rather than treating illegality as an inherent property of migrants.

proposed_edges.relationship: Shows immigration law reorganizing racial boundaries through quotas and categorical Asian exclusion.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Author’s quoted account and interview answers distinguish European national classifications from exclusions directed at Asians.

proposed_edges.relationship: Treats unauthorized immigration as a historically produced consequence of restriction and enforcement.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Interview examines1924 and1965 changes; it does not treat every migration history as the same or offer current legal guidance.
